name: llm-proxy
title: LLM Proxy
description: A server-side proxy for any OpenAI-compatible model, so your API key and your system prompt never reach the browser and every request has a cost ceiling.

env.description: The key the proxy calls the provider with. Stored write-only — it is never readable back, never sent to a browser, and never appears in a response.
env.where_to_find: OpenAI Platform → Dashboard → API keys → Create new secret key. It starts with sk-. Another OpenAI-compatible provider works too, but scaffolding authorises api.openai.com and nothing else — you would set OPENAI_BASE_URL and add that provider's host to the App's outbound allowlist first, or the call comes back as unreachable.

env.description: Comma-separated list of the websites allowed to call this endpoint from a browser, e.g. https://acme.com,https://www.acme.com. Leave blank to answer anything while you are developing, then set it before you go live.
env.where_to_find: The origin your frontend is served from — scheme and host, no path. Whatever appears in your browser's address bar before the first single slash.

post_deploy:
Your proxy is live at {{url}}

Call it from your frontend:
  fetch('{{url}}', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Where is my order?' }] }),
  })

Then:
  1. Edit src/system-prompt.ts — the shipped prompt is a placeholder persona, yours is the point.
  2. Lock the endpoint to your site:
       wawesome env set ALLOWED_ORIGINS https://your-site.com
  3. Watch what each request costs, in tokens, as it happens:
       wawesome logs --follow
  4. Shipped a bad prompt? Roll the Function back — no redeploy, no git revert.
